description.html: Cork bark comes from the cork oak and is one of the most widely used natural materials for decorating terrariums. The photo shows hollow, tube-shaped pieces with a rough, furrowed surface in gray-green and brown tones. Every piece is natural, so the shape and size vary from piece to piece.

Hollow and half-round pieces make a ready-made hide or tunnel for leopard geckos, snakes and other animals that hide near the ground. Arboreal species, such as crested geckos, use the bark for climbing and resting, because the rough surface gives their feet a good grip. Flatter pieces can be fixed to the back wall or placed as a platform on the warmer side of the terrarium.

Cork is lightweight, moisture-resistant and breaks down slowly, so it holds up well even in tropical terrariums with high humidity. It is compatible with bioactive setups and can be cut or broken into smaller pieces as needed.

Before placing the bark, rinse and brush it with lukewarm water to remove dust and debris from the surface, then let it dry. Place heavier pieces directly on the terrarium floor, under the substrate, so they do not shift when the animal digs. In humid terrariums, take the bark out from time to time, clean it with a brush and check that no mold has appeared on it.
